_why_this_file_is_the_gate: lane_git_town in scripts/capture_adapter_receipt.py reads this file before it decides anything else. Without it the lane emits SKIPPED_BY_POLICY and never starts the binary, which is the state the git-town lane carried while only a linux artifact was admitted. Deleting this file returns the lane to that refusal; nothing else has to be undone, and no other file grants execution.
channel: owner selection via AskUserQuestion in a live Claude Code session (goal: open-issue sweep), physicalized by agent-macro
what_was_asked: Authorize downloading git-town v24.0.0 darwin-arm64 from the official release, whose SHA-256 is already pinned in the owner's runtime-env catalog, and executing it in a disposable repository so the ninth adapter lane produces a receipt instead of an ABSENT record.
why_this_record_exists: skills/git-town-stacked-pr-worker/tests/live-git-town/admission.json admits a linux_intel_64 artifact at the same version number and declares platform linux. A different artifact is a different artifact: the version string is not the admitted identity, the digest is. This host is darwin/arm64, so the darwin asset needed its own decision rather than an install.

pin_authority.note: The catalog is upstream of this repository and read-only from here. This record admits the digest the catalog already pinned; it does not mint a new one.

derived_executable_identity.derivation: sha256 of the git-town member extracted from the admitted archive, after the archive's own sha256 was compared byte-for-byte with the catalog pin above.
derived_executable_identity.derived_by: agent-macro on 2026-08-17 while physicalizing this admission
derived_executable_identity.why_it_is_recorded_separately: The owner admitted an archive digest. The executable digest is an observation derived from that archive, not a second decision. The lane requires this value because it executes the member, not the archive, and a lane that checked only the archive would admit any binary someone left beside it.

scope: One capability: the stack-synchronization lane of scripts/capture_adapter_receipt.py, on a darwin/arm64 host, against a repository the lane creates and deletes under TMPDIR. Nothing else on this host is admitted to run this binary.
conditions: The executable is never installed system-wide, never placed on PATH by this repository, and never committed. Its path is supplied per run.
A sha256 that does not equal derived_executable_identity.sha256 is a refusal, not a warning: the lane records SKIPPED_BY_POLICY and does not start the process.
The lane runs only against a repository it creates under TMPDIR. Running git-town against this checkout, any worktree of it, or any branch of ed3c/skills-shared is outside this admission.
HOME, TMPDIR and the git config scope are redirected into the disposable tree so the binary's runlog and user configuration cannot escape it.
Sync runs with --no-push against a local bare remote. No network operation, forge token, propose or ship is admitted.
This record admits execution. It admits no evidence: whether the lane passed is decided by the receipt the capture writes, never by this file.
expiry: On any change to the admitted version, the catalog pin, or the archive digest. A different digest is a different artifact and needs its own decision; this record does not travel to one.
not_admitted_by_this_record: any git-town version other than 24.0.0, and any asset other than git-town_macos_arm_64.tar.gz
installing git-town on this host or adding it to PATH
running git-town against ed3c/skills-shared or any of its worktrees
any network-touching git-town command (propose, ship, repo, sync without --no-push)
promoting any lane whose measured gate outcome is NOT_ELIGIBLE; the owner explicitly did not select that option
the linux admission in skills/git-town-stacked-pr-worker, which is a separate record for a separate artifact and is unchanged by this one
